masteryZone.q: Who among the following is credited with founding the Indian National Congress?
masteryZone.sol: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British ICS officer, is credited as the founder of the Indian National Congress.

masteryZone.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in which city?
masteryZone.sol: The first session was held in Bombay at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College from December 28-31, 1885.

masteryZone.q: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
masteryZone.sol: W.C. Bonnerjee was the first President of the INC, presiding over the inaugural Bombay session in 1885.

masteryZone.q: The 'Safety Valve Theory' associates the formation of the INC with which of the following ideas?
opts: Channeling Indian political discontent to prevent rebellion
Establishing military alliances with Indian princes
Creating a cultural organization for Indian intellectuals
masteryZone.sol: The Safety Valve Theory suggests that A.O. Hume conceived the INC as a channel for Indian discontent to prevent another outbreak like 1857.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following pre-INC organizations contributed to the formation of the Indian National Congress? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: All four organizations were pre-INC political bodies that laid the groundwork for a national political organization. The Landholders' Society (1836), Bombay Association (1852), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870), and Indian Association (1876) were all precursors to the INC.

masteryZone.q: The first session of the INC was held in Calcutta in 1885.
masteryZone.sol: False. The first session was held in Bombay at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College.

masteryZone.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 during the viceroyalty of Lord Dufferin.
masteryZone.sol: True. Lord Dufferin was Viceroy of India from 1884 to 1888 when the INC was formed.

masteryZone.q: The first session of the INC in 1885 was attended by ______ delegates.
masteryZone.sol: 72 delegates attended the first INC session in Bombay in 1885.

masteryZone.q: The first session of the INC was held at the ______ Sanskrit College in Bombay.
masteryZone.sol: The first INC session was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.

masteryZone.q: The INC was formed in ______, which is 1885.
masteryZone.sol: The INC was formed in December 1885 with its first session from December 28-31.

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress?
masteryZone.sol: Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President of the INC (Madras Session, 1887).

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Englishman to become the President of the INC?
masteryZone.sol: George Yule was the first English President of the INC (Allahabad Session, 1888).

masteryZone.q: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over which session of the INC?
masteryZone.sol: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the 2nd Session of the INC held in Calcutta in 1886.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sessions of the INC were presided over by Indian leaders? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Sessions 1, 2, and 3 were presided over by Indian leaders. The 4th session in 1888 was presided over by George Yule, who was English.

masteryZone.q: George Yule was the first Christian President of the INC.
masteryZone.sol: Technically true that Yule was Christian, but he is more specifically known as the first English President of the INC.

masteryZone.q: Pherozeshah Mehta served as the President of the INC for two consecutive sessions (1889 and 1890).
masteryZone.sol: True. Pherozeshah Mehta presided over the 5th (Bombay, 1889) and 6th (Calcutta, 1890) sessions.

masteryZone.q: The 7th session of the INC (1891) was held in ______, with A. Webb as President.
masteryZone.sol: The 7th INC session was held in Nagpur in 1891 - the first time INC met in Central India.

masteryZone.q: The 4th session of the INC was held in ______ in 1888.
masteryZone.sol: The 4th session was held in Allahabad in 1888, presided over by George Yule.

masteryZone.q: Which year was the first INC session held in Calcutta?
masteryZone.sol: 1886 (2nd Session, presided by Dadabhai Naoroji).

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Parsi President of the INC?
masteryZone.sol: Dadabhai Naoroji (2nd Session, Calcutta, 1886).

masteryZone.q: The period from 1885 to 1905 in the history of INC is known as which phase?
masteryZone.sol: The period from 1885 to 1905 is known as the Moderate Phase. Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, Gokhale, and Pherozeshah Mehta dominated this period.

masteryZone.q: What was the primary method of political struggle adopted by the Moderate leaders of the INC?
masteryZone.sol: The Moderates used constitutional agitation, prayers, petitions, and protests, believing in the British sense of justice.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was a significant achievement of Moderate politics. Who was the Viceroy when this Act was passed?
masteryZone.sol: Lord Lansdowne (1888-1894) was the Viceroy when the Indian Councils Act 1892 was passed.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following were key demands of the Moderate phase of the INC? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Moderates demanded Indianization of civil services, expansion of legislative councils, and repeal of repressive acts like the Arms Act. Complete independence was not a Moderate demand.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following leaders were part of the Moderate faction of the INC? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Gokhale, Banerjee, and Mehta were Moderate leaders. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Extremist leader.

masteryZone.q: The Moderates of the INC demanded 'Swaraj' (self-rule) as their immediate goal.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Moderates sought constitutional reforms within the British Empire, not immediate Swaraj. The Extremists led by Tilak were the first to demand Swaraj.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act 1892 introduced direct elections for the first time in India.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Act introduced the principle of election, but elections were indirect. Direct elections were introduced later.

masteryZone.q: The 'politics of 3 P's' associated with Moderates refers to Prayers, Petitions, and ______.
masteryZone.sol: The 3 P's of Moderate politics were Prayers, Petitions, and Protests.

masteryZone.q: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in the year ______.
masteryZone.sol: The Servants of India Society was founded in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

masteryZone.q: Which Constitutional Act increased the size of legislative councils but fell short of Congress demands?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act 1892.

masteryZone.q: Who is known as the 'political guru' of Mahatma Gandhi?
masteryZone.sol: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Moderate phase of the INC (1885-1905) failed to achieve meaningful political concessions from the British government.
Reason (R): The Moderates relied solely on constitutional methods of prayer, petition, and protest.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. The limited success of the Moderate method of constitutional petitions led to the rise of the Extremist school demanding more assertive methods.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Moderates dominated the INC from 1885 to 1905.
Reason (R): The Moderates believed in the justice and fair play of the British government.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. However, the Moderates' dominance was due to their organizational strength and the initial absence of organized opposition, not solely due to their faith in British justice.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Moderate phase eventually give way to the Extremist phase in the INC?
masteryZone.sol: The Moderate phase gave way to the Extremist phase because: (1) The constitutional methods of prayers and petitions failed to achieve substantial political reforms. (2) The Partition of Bengal (1905) intensified nationalist anger. (3) Leaders like Tilak, Pal, and Lajpat Rai advocated for mass mobilization, boycotts, and Swaraj instead of petitions. (4) The lack of meaningful concessions from the British exposed the limitations of Moderate politics.

masteryZone.q: How did the Indian Councils Act 1892 impact the Indian national movement?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act 1892 increased the number of nominated non-official members in legislative councils and introduced an indirect election system. While the INC welcomed this as a step towards representation, the Act fell far short of demands for a truly representative government. It strengthened the Moderate faith in constitutional reform temporarily, but the limitations of the Act also sowed seeds for more assertive nationalism.

masteryZone.q: Explain the 'Safety Valve Theory' and 'Nationalist Theory' regarding the formation of the INC.
masteryZone.sol: The Safety Valve Theory, propagated by the British historian Sir John Strachey, suggests that A.O. Hume founded the INC with the encouragement of Lord Dufferin to provide a 'safety valve' for the growing political discontent among the Indian middle class, thereby preventing another rebellion like 1857. The Nationalist Theory counters this by arguing that the INC was a natural outcome of India's political awakening, and Indian leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji and Pherozeshah Mehta independently aspired for a national organization. Hume only facilitated what Indian nationalism was already destined to create.
